text.aria-label: Title text 'Negative differences favour radiation-corrected inputs'
Title text 'Figure 2: Radiation correction lowers solar forecast loss'

g.text: Figure 2: Radiation correction lowers solar forecast loss

text.aria-label: Subtitle text 'Same production training settings; loss with radiation-corrected inputs minus loss with old inputs. Forecasting models retrained on past data; forecasts scored July 2025–June 2026. Predictions near to and far from issuance are combined. Both versions predict power for the same meters at the same times. Three training runs use different random choices during training. A seed sets those choices. Forecasts describe possible power outputs and their probabilities. Loss scores those predicted probabilities against observed power. Recalculations repeatedly select whole months and a seed shared by both forecasts. Months can be selected more than once in a recalculation. The line covers the middle 95% of the resulting loss differences. “All series” combines demand meters, solar farms, and wind farms. Loss differences are percentage points of each meter's frozen capacity. Capacity is a fixed power scale: the 99th percentile of each meter's absolute power readings. The scale uses the full available history, including readings after the scored period. Dot: mean loss difference on matched forecasts. Line: 95% interval from repeated draws of whole months and one matched training seed. More negative loss differences favour radiation-corrected inputs. All rows are planned: written into the study plan before any result existed.'
